dedupe_keys.name: idlib low carbon municipal solid waste network design for a post conflict recovering city milp

description: This case study designs the municipal solid waste network of a city rebuilding after conflict, tested in Idlib Governorate, Syria. The authors published it as an open-access journal article. A policy-driven mixed-integer linear programming model chooses transfer stations, mechanical-biological treatment plants, waste-to-energy plants and landfills while weighing four goals together: total cost, carbon emissions, implementation feasibility risk and site environmental risk, and it compares three carbon policies, a carbon tax, a carbon tax with a processing subsidy, and cap-and-trade. Coverage is Idlib Governorate. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives licence. Caveats: input data are limited in a post-conflict setting, the risk scores involve judgement, and the network is a planning design, not a built system. The study found that the share of waste sent to waste-to-energy has the strongest effect on emissions and energy recovery, while the policy scenarios mainly change costs: the carbon tax raises the monetised cost of emissions, subsidies reduce treatment costs, and cap-and-trade creates permit costs or revenue depending on the cap. Simulation uses: an example of optimisation for investment appraisal and recovery of waste infrastructure after conflict. Related records: SwolfPy (model-swolfpy) optimises waste systems with life-cycle assessment, and the World Bank What a Waste database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) gives comparable waste statistics.
